terra.problem: “No sharing, no asking” adds details the passage does not give.
“The altar never got a turn” goes beyond what the text says about what the fork brought up.
The comparison to leftovers makes the LORD’s offering the subject of a food comparison.
“Fear would've changed this whole story” presents an unsupported guess as fact.
The explanation is flat and repetitive, with little of Papa Dorin’s personality.
It states that Eli is not happy without marking his feeling as a guess.
It asserts that Eli’s question was meant to make his sons stop and think, but the text does not give that reason.
“They kept going” asserts what the sons did after the warning. The text says they did not listen.
“I won't joke about it” comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage.
“Out of every tribe” suggests a selection from each tribe. The text says Eli’s father was selected out of all the tribes.
“It’s meant to be” adds an unstated purpose to the LORD’s words.
Calling Hophni and Phinehas priests at Shiloh needs a reference to 1 Samuel 1:3, outside this passage.
“They used to grab the best of the meat” treats the people left in Eli’s house as the same people who took the offerings. The text does not say that.
“Trying to get back into” priestly work assumes the people left in Eli’s house previously held priestly offices.
